description: JSI TRIGA Mark II core geometry from open sources only (no ICSBEP). Values from other GA TRIGA Mark II reactors are marked as such; the JSI-specific ones win where both exist.

sources.svajger2024: I. Švajger et al., Nuclear Engineering and Technology 56 (2024) 1165–1203, doi:10.1016/j.net.2023.11.021
sources.ksu2004: Kansas State University TRIGA Mark II, Safety Analysis Report dated 2004-12-21 (NRC license R-88; public, NRC ADAMS). Standard GA stainless-steel TRIGA element and components; a different reactor, so reactor-specific values (reflector size, rod types) are not used for JSI
sources.trigapulse: JSI TRIGA pulse database, trigapulse.ijs.si: core maps 242.pdf and 246.pdf, rod tables s242.pdf and s246.pdf (downloaded, kept out of git)
sources.castagna2017: C. Castagna et al., A new model with Serpent for the first criticality benchmarks of the TRIGA Mark II reactor, arXiv:1707.05194 (Pavia reactor)
sources.ravnik: M. Ravnik, Description of TRIGA Reactor (JSI Reactor Infrastructure Centre), ric.ijs.si/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Description_TRIGA_Reactor.pdf. JSI's own description; preferred over the other reactors' documents
sources.uta: University of Texas at Austin TRIGA, Safety Analysis Report (redacted), NRC ADAMS ML23279A146 (standard GA rod travel)
sources.merljak2015: V. Merljak, JSI TRIGA 3D Reactor Model: Transition to Cartesian Geometry and Sample Kinetic Simulations, NENE 2015, paper 306

grid.ringRadiiStatus: ravnik Table 1 (ring diameters in inches, rounded to 0.1 in); rings pass through element centres

ringRadiiCandidateCm.status: Unverified finer values (4.05 ... 19.89 cm) from a web-search summary of JSI slides; agree with ravnik within the inch rounding. ravnik is used.

reflector.check: 17.9/2 in = 22.733 cm minus 0.25 in casing = 22.098 cm = svajger2024's radius to the reflector

gridPlates.spacingStatus: castagna2017 gives 64.8 cm for Pavia; not confirmed for JSI

fuelElement.source: ravnik Table 4 (radial details from svajger2024 Table 1 are used where finer)
fuelElement.note: JSI end reflectors (2.6 in top, 3.7 in bottom) differ from ksu2004's 3.44 in each; JSI values are used

controlRods.travelSource: uta (standard GA rod travel 15 in); also castagna2017 (38.1 cm over 705 steps)

stepCm.derivation: (900 - 200) steps over 38.1 cm; matches castagna2017's ~0.054 cm/step
stepCm.transient: ASSUMED the same 0.0544 cm/step (castagna2017: 47.2 cm over 873 steps = 0.0541); transient travel not stated for JSI

244.source: trigapulse s246.pdf header (measured 2021-06-08 on core 244; core 246's pulses use this table)
